properties.global_prompt:
Photorealistic live-action first-century biblical drama. Match each supplied starting image for exact character identity, wardrobe, time of day, location and lighting. Each timeline segment is one continuous take; cuts between segments carry changes of viewpoint or time. Use restrained human performances and purposeful smooth camera movement at natural real-time speed. Preserve prop ownership and completed actions. properties.local_prompts:
One continuous 12-second live-action shot. Begin directly from the supplied image. Night in the supplied mirrorless rented room: bed against left wall beneath the square window, fixed wooden garment peg beside the right-hand doorway, one clay oil lamp on the stone shelf. Father’s fine russet mantle hangs intact on that peg. Younger stands center in a light mantle with a narrow blue border, holding its edge to judge the fall over his ordinary tunic. Bedroll and money are near the bed; repaired waterskin hangs at his hip.

Camera: Small dolly from room center toward the door, following his preparation to leave.
Action: Over the following weeks: younger tests the fall of his purchased blue-bordered mantle by feel in the mirrorless room, then leaves satisfied. Russet remains hanging as a quiet reminder of home.
End state: Same lamplit room, younger now at the partly open doorway with his hand on the timber door edge and a satisfied private expression, the new light mantle falling neatly with its narrow blue border visible. The russet gift remains on the same peg behind him. His repaired waterskin and pouch leave with him; bedding stays by the bed. No mirror anywhere.
Performance and dialogue: No dialogue. Characters remain silent.
Only the explicitly assigned dialogue is spoken once by its named speaker; all other descriptions are acting directions, never narration. Keep speaking faces large and sharp, with natural synchronized lips and pauses. Maintain a single continuous take and consistent movement speed.
Continuity: First on-body blue-bordered wardrobe state; russet hangs on fixed peg. Room geography: left window/bed, right peg/door, oil lamp shelf. No mirror or generated text. Younger still adequately fed.

overall_soundscape: Natural sound belonging to this location and the visible action: restrained cloth and footsteps, appropriate room tone or outdoor air; animals and objects only where present. Sound falls off with distance. Retain explicitly described sound cues above. No invented speech, vocal loops or chanting.
non_diegetic_music: N/A | One continuous 12-second live-action shot. Begin directly from the supplied image. Night version of the same tavern court, illuminated by modest clay oil lamps under the reed shade. Younger, now wearing the light blue-bordered mantle, counts silver into the host’s open palm at foreground right. Behind them one foreign pipe player raises a pipe while the hand drummer waits. Fully clothed guests talk across one another at benches, laughter uneven rather than theatrical.

Camera: Short lateral drift between host’s hand and the musicians, retaining younger in foreground.
Action: Pipe tests a note and hand drum answers. Host extends his palm; younger pays for the gathering and adds more for the musicians. Host’s attention warms immediately while guests overlap in natural chatter.
End state: Same uninterrupted medium-wide, younger adds a further coin toward the musicians while the host’s face has turned immediately warm and attentive. The foreign pipe player is poised after a first note and the drummer’s hand hovers over the drum skin. Guests remain at the same benches; younger’s repaired waterskin hangs beside his seat.
Performance and dialogue: No dialogue. Characters remain silent.
Only the explicitly assigned dialogue is spoken once by its named speaker; all other descriptions are acting directions, never narration. Keep speaking faces large and sharp, with natural synchronized lips and pauses. Maintain a single continuous take and consistent movement speed.
Continuity: Same court relit for night; no relocation or lavish palace. One pipe player, one hand drummer; period instruments only. Silver amount unspecified; warm attention follows payment. Light mantle narrow blue border still initially unstained.

Lamplit banquet court, younger and Damon in a simple turning dance near the bench, with their hands loosely joined at ordinary human reach. Younger wears the light mantle with a narrow blue border and looks attentively at Damon’s footwork. The familiar fully clothed companions watch from their benches, modest smiles rather than extravagant revelry.

Camera: Gentle half-orbit around two turning dancers at walking speed; fixed screen axis and natural balance.
Action: Damon draws younger into the turning dance. Younger misses a step; everyone laughs, including him. Camera remains with the awkward, enjoyable moment; music and laughter carry it.
End state: Same continuous dance after a restrained partial camera orbit, younger has just missed a step and steadied himself with one foot planted wide. He is laughing naturally at his error; Damon laughs with him and gives him space. Companions respond with uneven smiles and laughter. No fall, acrobatics or sexualized action.
Performance and dialogue: No dialogue. Characters remain silent.

Used clay cups and dishes remain scattered on the same table. His light mantle shows the narrow blue border stained red at the edge; oil lamps burn low, leaving the doorway dark.
